clue.text: Winner to embrace old French writer

parts.note: a victor is a winner
to embrace someone is to hug them

explanation.surface: A champion is urged to hug some French author of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Les Misérables and The Hunchback of Notre-Dame was a celebrated nineteenth-century French novelist and poet.

clue.text: Perhaps a solemn promise by the Spanish

parts.note: a vow is a solemn promise
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Maybe a solemn promise is made by the Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps a' looks like the start of a phrase, but it is the definition: the letter A is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter A is one of the five vowel letters in the English alphabet, so it exemplifies the answer.

clue.text: Best item on dinner table at Christmas? A sort of biscuit

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

parts.words: item on dinner table at Christmas
parts.note: a Christmas cracker is a paper tube pulled apart with a bang at British Christmas dinners

explanation.surface: The finest festive table item turns out to be a kind of biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a paper tube containing a small gift and a joke, pulled with a snap at British Christmas meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream cracker is a crisp, unsweetened British biscuit usually eaten with cheese.

clue.text: Ruminant animals lacking good cereal grass

indicators.note: the animals are without the letter for good, so it is removed

parts.note: goats are cud-chewing ruminants

explanation.surface: Cud-chewing beasts are short of decent grazing.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cultivated cereal plant of the grass family grown for its grain.

clue.text: Type of dog, slippery creature, grabbed by that lady

indicators.note: the creature is held by the lady, so it goes inside her letters

parts.note: her refers to that lady
an eel is a notoriously slippery fish

explanation.surface: A dog breed and a slippery eel are seized by some woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A heeler is a cattle dog that herds by nipping at heels, like the Australian blue heeler.

clue.text: Part of mathematics test beneath George and myself

indicators.note: in a down answer the test sits beneath the other pieces, so it comes last

parts.note: Geo. is a traditional abbreviation of the name George
me refers to myself
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: A maths exam is taken below George and me.
explanation.walkthrough: Geo. is an old written abbreviation of George, seen on coins and letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry is the branch of maths dealing with shapes, lines, angles and space.

clue.text: Food shop to reproach lady removing contents on purpose

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared foods
to berate is to scold or reproach

indicators.note: taking away the inside of the word leaves only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A deli worker scolds a woman for emptying the shelves on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately means intentionally, with full awareness of what one is doing.

clue.text: Loosely hang fish at end of day

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod

explanation.surface: Someone lets a line hang slack while fishing at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at end of' puts ANGLE after D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle is to hang or swing loosely, as legs over the side of a pier.

clue.text: Struggle with awful sleet on river

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece sitting on another follows it, so the sleet letters come after the river
awful suggests something messed up, so the letters of sleet are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone battles foul sleety weather beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is easily read as a link, but here it supplies its abbreviation W.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrestle is to grapple or contend, so it serves as a verb for struggle.

clue.text: Ring huge Greek character

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
mega is slang for huge

explanation.surface: A boxing ring holds an enormous Greek fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Plain meal regularly selected somewhere in Peru

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of these words is chosen

explanation.surface: A simple dinner was picked out at a restaurant in Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of PLAIN MEAL give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru, so it is indeed a place within that country.

clue.text: Parting sports arena after Ballesteros maybe

indicators.note: the arena comes after the golfer's first name in the answer

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros was a famous Spanish golfer, so Seve is a name he exemplifies
a ring is an arena for boxing or wrestling

explanation.surface: A sports venue is left behind following a famous golfer's departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parting' looks like a farewell noun but works as the verb form, meaning cutting apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Severing means cutting off or separating, the same as parting as a verb form.

clue.text: Unusual article about new musical instrument

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes about, or around, the letter for new
unusual signals the letters of article are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A strange piece is written about a new instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges ARTICLE into CLARIET, and 'about' puts it around N.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a single-reed woodwind instrument played in orchestras and jazz bands.

clue.text: Mountainous region, to the west, Mallory traversed partly

indicators.note: in an across answer going west means reading right to left, so the hidden letters run backwards
only part of these two words is taken, so the answer lies hidden across them

explanation.surface: The climber Mallory crossed part of a mountain area heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' picks LORYT out of malLORY Traversed, and 'to the west' reads it backwards. George Mallory was a British mountaineer lost on Everest in 1924.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine area straddling Austria and Italy, famously full of mountains.

clue.text: Small earthquake damaged Metro railway primarily

indicators.note: damaged suggests something broken up, so the letters of metro are rearranged
primarily means first, so the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A minor quake has damaged the underground railway system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges METRO into TREMO, and 'primarily' adds the R of railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a slight shaking of the ground, a minor seismic event.

clue.text: Chief magistrate once concerned with first woman

parts.note: re means about or concerning
in the Bible Eve was the first woman

explanation.surface: An old-time magistrate was worried about the original woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was the chief officer or magistrate of a town or district in Anglo-Saxon and medieval England.

clue.text: One-time pro associated with French sea

parts.note: pro means for, as in pros and cons
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A once professional player is linked with the French coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Former, like one-time, describes something or someone that was so in the past.

clue.text: Snail Charlie found amongst storage at sea

indicators.note: the letter is found among the others, so it sits inside them
being at sea means confused, so the letters of storage are mixed up

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A snail called Charlie turned up in the hold of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges STORAGE into ESARGOT, and 'found amongst' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French word for snail, used in English for snails served as food.

clue.text: Hospital member suffering

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
an arm is a limb, and member is an old word for a limb

explanation.surface: A member of a hospital board is in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm, as a noun, is injury or damage, so it can stand for suffering inflicted on someone.

clue.text: Little child obtains right headwear

indicators.note: the child gets the letter inside, holding it

parts.note: a mite is an affectionate word for a small child

explanation.surface: A small child gets the correct hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall pointed ceremonial hat worn by bishops.

clue.text: Brave man in the rocket

indicators.note: the answer sits inside these words, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A courageous astronaut sits aboard the spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a person admired for courage, so a brave man fits as a description.

clue.text: Classical theatre Oswald's outside a very long time

indicators.note: only the outside of the name is used, its first and last letters

parts.note: an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: Oswald has been out of an old theatre for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' takes the first and last letters of Oswald, OD; the 's is a link standing for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeon was an ancient Greek or Roman building for musical performances, a classical sort of theatre.

clue.text: Part of sailing ship contains something woolly and life jacket

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: a mast is part of a sailing ship
a ewe is a female sheep, which is covered in wool

explanation.surface: Part of a sailing ship holds woolly clothing and a buoyancy aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Second World War airmen nicknamed their inflatable life vest after the buxom film star Mae West.

clue.text: Conventional image of potter, eyes fixed

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rearranged or doctored, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The usual picture of a potter is someone with eyes fixed on the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype is an oversimplified, widely held picture of a type of person.
